title: AI is turning the Smithsonian into an illuminated fever dream

paragraphs.text: The National Mall has become a hot spot for festivities this summer as the U.S. commemorates its 250th anniversary, hosting the (sparsely attended) Great American State Fair as well as a massive FIFA fan zone for the World Cup. The latest celebration arriving at the capital’s famous park is set to illuminate the red sandstone facade of the Smithsonian.
paragraphs.translation: 國家廣場今年夏天已成為慶祝活動的熱點，因為美國正紀念其 250 週年，舉辦了（參與人數稀少的）大美國州博覽會以及世界盃的大型 FIFA 粉絲區。抵達首都著名公園的最新慶祝活動將照亮史密森尼學會的紅砂岩外牆。

paragraphs.text: For the immersive public installation titled Smithsonian Dreams, the artist Refik Anadol will project images from the museum’s collection, as well as abstract graphics made with the help of AI, onto the Smithsonian’s Gothic Revival building.
paragraphs.translation: 為了這個名為《史密森尼之夢》的沉浸式公共藝術裝置，藝術家 Refik Anadol 將把來自博物館館藏的影像，以及在 AI 幫助下製作的抽象圖形，投影到史密森尼學會的哥德復興式建築上。

paragraphs.text: Lisa Sasaki, deputy under secretary for special projects at the Smithsonian Institution, tells Fast Company that Anadol’s work was guided by a question: “The Smithsonian Castle, if it could dream, what would it dream about?”
paragraphs.translation: 史密森尼學會特殊專案副次長 Lisa Sasaki 告訴《Fast Company》，Anadol 的作品是受到一個問題的啟發：「如果史密森尼城堡會做夢，它會夢到什麼？」

paragraphs.text: With more than 2 million library volumes, 156,000 cubic feet of archival materials (the size of two Boeing 737-800 airliners), and some 157 million objects and specimens, the Smithsonian Institution is one of the world’s largest repositories of knowledge. Using a custom artificial intelligence system, Anadol dove into almost 200 years of digitized items ranging over photographs, art, manuscripts, scientific records, objects, and even physical specimens.
paragraphs.translation: 史密森尼學會擁有超過 200 萬冊圖書館藏書、15.6 萬立方英尺的檔案材料（相當於兩架波音 737-800 客機的大小），以及約 1.57 億件物品和標本，是世界上最大的知識庫之一。利用自定義的人工智慧系統，Anadol 深入研究了近 200 年的數位化項目，範圍涵蓋照片、藝術品、手稿、科學記錄、物品甚至物理標本。

paragraphs.text: Treating these elements as data points, Anadol created a UMAP (uniform manifold approximation and projection), mapping the connections between the data.
paragraphs.translation: Anadol 將這些元素視為數據點，創建了一個 UMAP（均勻流形逼近與投影），繪製出數據之間的聯繫。

paragraphs.text: “For me, data is a form of memory,” Anadol said in a press statement. “Using machine intelligence as a creative collaborator, we are transforming the archive into a living experience where history, culture, science and imagination continuously unfold in new ways.”
paragraphs.translation: Anadol 在一份新聞聲明中表示：「對我來說，數據是記憶的一種形式。利用機器智能作為創意合作者，我們正在將檔案轉化為一種活生生的體驗，讓歷史、文化、科學和想像力不斷以新的方式展現。」

paragraphs.text: Projected on the 145-foot-tall building, the installation will run for only two nights, July 17 and 18. To transform the castle, the installation is using Panasonic projection technology to showcase the artist’s immersive presentation as a show with visuals and sounds.
paragraphs.translation: 該裝置投影在 145 英尺高的建築上，僅展出兩個晚上，即 7 月 17 日和 18 日。為了改造城堡，該裝置使用 Panasonic 的投影技術，將藝術家的沉浸式展示呈現為一場結合視覺與聽覺的表演。
